messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Stan 1.0.3 Released
parts:
The Stan Development Team is happy to announce the
availability of Stan and RStan versions 1.0.3. See:

http://mc-stan.org/

Stan now supports lower and upper bounds in vector and
matrix declarations and vectorization of all univariate
continuous probability functions.

RStan now supports running chains in multiple processes
and merging the results.

We've also fixed some bugs and hopefully made user error
messages more comprehensible.

The important issues dealt with in the release are as follows.


v 1.0.3 Release Notes (25 Oct 2012)
======================================================================
Stan Bug Fixes:
-- error output in stanc now directed to standard error
-- catching all exceptions thrown in stanc to prevent core dumps
-- parser now accepts variable names starting with "int" and "real"
in first assignment after declaration
-- now catching unknown truncation cdfs and vectorizations in stanc
-- (hopefully) less scary message for domain error rejects
-- removed use of assert(); replaced with exceptions where
appropriate
-- fixed boundary condition on reporting max init retry failures
-- fixed initialization errors in tests that failed on some platforms
-- improved error checking for matrix size args to prevent segfaults
-- fixed boundary condition on bounded transform to allow
beta(0.8,0.8) samples near 0 or 1
Stan New Features:
-- mdivide_left_tri_low, mdivide_right_tri_low functions
-- all univariate continuous densities vectorized
-- better error checking for transforms
-- new error return type in stanc for invalid arguments
-- lower and upper bounds for vectors, row vectors, and matrices
-- command parameter refresh <= 0 turns off iteration reporting
-- int divisions produce warnings in stanc
-- errors caused by invalid transformed parameters include var name
-- various efficiency improvements and error handling for boundary
conditions and special cases of probability functions
-- simplified matrix code with heavier use of templating
Stan Manual Additions:
-- example of defining new distribution with parameters
-- diff report vs. previous versions
-- updated for range constraints on vector, row vector, matrix
-- updated Eigen licensing information (now MPL, was LGPL)
-- fixed alpha ordering issue in function index due to bolding
RStan Bug Fixes:
-- bug of setting parameter epsilon_pm wrongly for NUTS
-- fixed seed reset so results match Stan
RStan New Features:
-- return empty stanfit object upon error such as incorrect data
input, wrong argument specification, etc. Previously, it will
stop. The empty stanfit includes the compiled model, so it can be
reused.
-- add function stan_demo() to run examples included in Stan.
-- add function sflist2stanfit() to merge a list of stanfit objects
into one, to facilitate user-level parallelism.
-- add S3 method as.matrix, as.array, is.array, dim,
dimnames for stanfit objects.
-- specify seed using string of digits in addition to numbers
-- turn off refresh if value <= 0
======================================================================

As usual, let us know on the users list or on our issue tracker
if there are problems.

- Stan Development Team

messages.author: 33d5534e21fbbe0f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan 1.0.3 Released
parts:
Hello stan developers,  I attach an Rstan script and some sample data.   You've already generously provided me with feedback on model constructions over more complex versions.   So I send this note to suggest that this model should not fail under Rstan 1.0.3, but it does; actually, it crashes the R session.   I'm not asking for debugging help, but thought it may be useful for you to have an example of a model that absolutely will not run in stan (where variations of it do under BUGS solvers).   The model augments the data likelihood over multiple statements under differing data types.   The multiple data blocks express a dependence through sharing a common set of multivariate nested random effects.   Each random effect term is multivariate on a set of latent indices so that the 'rows' are each sampled in a multivariate fashion.   I've employed one of the stan developer tricks to avoid repeated inversion and gradient computation and storing over multiple NUTS steps for the covariance matrices over repeated sampling draws of the multivariate random effects.   Anyway, my guess is that the repeated sampling of a multivariate latent object is the problem.   While I've seen implementations of stan models on the list that perform a single multivariate parameters draw, I've not seen any that perform multiple such draws.   But i don't know.   At this point, I'm quite sure the issue isn't the model concept or the data and I suspect the model triggers a stan bug.  It bears brief mention that the same problem persists, no matter the prior formulations and their degree of informativeness.

Terrance.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan 1.0.3 Released
parts:
Hi Terrance,

If you follow the procedure for a runtime error at

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/4gv3fNCqSNk/FXHj6fn0SC0J

then (even without gdb) the (or at least, a) problem is apparent:

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/tmp/SU/tds$ ./ordMultiProt_E_test --data=datstan_mp.Rdump

Exception: INDEX OPERATOR [] OUT OF BOUNDS; index=1215; lower bound=1; upper bound=1214; index position=1; c3

Diagnostic information: 
Dynamic exception type: std::out_of_range
std::exception::what: INDEX OPERATOR [] OUT OF BOUNDS; index=1215; lower bound=1; upper bound=1214; index position=1; c3


So, one of your loops goes to c3[1215] when it only has 1214 rows. A quick grep reveals

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/tmp/SU/tds$ grep -n c3 ordMultiProt_E_test.stan 
101:    matrix[N2,D3] c3;
128:            for( i in 1:N3 ) for( d in 1:D3 ) c3[i,d]       <- Delta[teacher3[i],(D1+D2+d)] + Phi[section3[i],(D1+D2+d)] + Theta[session3[i],(D1+D2+d)] + Beta[rater3[i],(D1+D2+d)];
159:    for(i in 1:N3) for(d in 1:D3) y3[i,d]   ~ ordered_logistic(c3[i,d],gamma3[d]);


So, you are looping to N3 but c3 has only N2 rows.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: index o.o.b. exception + RStan error reporting
parts: Ben wrote this:

> goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/tmp/SU/tds$ ./ordMultiProt_E_test --data=datstan_mp.Rdump
>
> Exception: INDEX OPERATOR [] OUT OF BOUNDS; index=1215; lower bound=1; upper bound=1214; index position=1; c3
>
> Diagnostic information:
> Dynamic exception type: std::out_of_range
> std::exception::what: INDEX OPERATOR [] OUT OF BOUNDS; index=1215; lower bound=1; upper bound=1214; index position=1; c3

1. I should've paid more attention to Ben's output.
It's good that Stan's picking up the error -- this is
what it's supposed to do.

Is the exception causing RStan to crash? If so, we
probably just need to put a catch in the appropriate place
to write the exception's type and message back to the R stderr
stream.

I'm not sure what happens during I/O. Our message could
be a lot better in terms of identifying what was going on
when the error occurred (I/O or model, specifically).

As is, I only know from looking at the code that it arose
when some function called stan::math::raise_range_error,
which throws a std::out_of_range exception.

2. I'd like to figure out a simpler policy for RStan user
error reporting than having them run through Stan command
line. It just seems like too much of an installation and
manual reading exercise for an error report.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: index o.o.b. exception + RStan error reporting
parts:
On Saturday, October 27, 2012 6:27:22 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
2.  I'd like to figure out a simpler policy for RStan user
error reporting than having them run through Stan command
line.  It just seems like too much of an installation and
manual reading exercise for an error report.

If the exception doesn't take down the R process, then the message should  get back to the R process eventually. I think in v1.0.1, R may have been crashing before the error flushed. This may vary depending on what GUI the user is accessing R from.

Ben

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: index o.o.b. exception + RStan error reporting
parts:
I did not try this example.  But tried a simple one:

parameters {
    real y[1];
}

model {
    y[2] ~ normal(0, 1);
}


In RStan, if we set_cppo('debug'), R would not crash for this example.  set_cppo('debug') would not set -DNDEBUG flag. By default, Stan does not set this flag.  If -DNDEBUG is set in Stan, Stan will exit with a segfault for this example.  

When set_cppo('debug') is set in RStan, for this example, R would not crash. 

> set_cppo('debug')
mode debug for compiling C++ code is set
> 
> scode <- '
+ parameters {
+ real y[1];
+ }
+ 

+ model {
+ y[2] ~ normal(0, 1);
+ }
+ '

>
> library(rstan)
> a <- stan(model_code = scode, iter = 10, chains = 1)
TRANSLATING MODEL 'scode' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'scode' NOW.
SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'scode' NOW (CHAIN 1).
Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) : 

  INDEX OPERATOR [] OUT OF BOUNDS; index=2; lower bound=1; upper bound=1; index position=1; y

error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

> 

Last, just a reminder: when set_cppo set the mode as debug, it would stay in that mode.  So remember to change that back to 'fast' mode if 'debug' mode is not needed any more. 

--
Jiqiang

In RStan, if we set_cppo('debug'), R would not crash for this example.  set_cppo('debug') would not set -DNDEBUG flag. By default, Stan does not set this flag.
